title: Core server runs, with the Plan module behind it
body:
**PRD:** d-one-server, d-mod-manifest, d-mod-api, d-mod-view, d-sec-local, n-node-builtin

## What to build

One local server starts and serves modules. The first module is Plan: the mind map and the documents work exactly as today, but through the core server, with Plan's API under `/api/plan/`. Plan plugs in through a minimal module contract: a manifest (id, name, version), server endpoints and a view.

The restructuring this needs is part of this ticket, not a separate step. Today, reading and writing the map and merging browser saves live inside one request handler of Plan's server, while the CLI and the hook reach the same file their own way. That logic moves into one module with a small interface (read, apply ops, save from the browser, take human edits). The CLI, the hook and the core server all use it.

Today Plan's server listens on every network interface and does not check the `Host` header. The core server ends that.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One command starts the core server; the Plan view opens, the map can be edited and the documents are generated as before
- [ ] Plan's endpoints are under `/api/plan/`
- [ ] Plan registers with the core through a manifest (id, name, version)
- [ ] The server listens on `127.0.0.1` only and answers a foreign `Host` header with 403
- [ ] Only Node built-in modules are used; nothing to install
- [ ] The groundwork-prd-maker hook and skill still work
- [ ] `.claude/launch.json`, the hook setting and the README show the new way to start
- [ ] The implementation links of "done" items on the map point to the current `modules/` paths
- [ ] Reading, writing and merging the map live in one module; the CLI, the hook and the server use it
- [ ] The merge has `node --test` tests through that module's interface (Claude and the browser write at the same time; the browser saves on top of an old version)
- [ ] The `Host` check and the `127.0.0.1` binding are covered by a test

## Blocked by

- None (can start immediately)

title: The core grants write access; Plan state moves to .groundwork/plan/
body:
**PRD:** d-mod-writes, d-sec-write, d-state-dir

## What to build

Every module names the folders it may write to, and nothing else can be written. Modules do not get general file system access: the core hands each module a writer that can only write under the folders its manifest names. A forbidden write is not filtered out afterwards; there is simply no way to make it. Writes are possible only under `docs/product/` and `.groundwork/`.

Plan's local state (browser edits Claude has not read yet) moves from today's `.prd-maker/` to `.groundwork/plan/`; existing state is kept.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The module's manifest lists the folders it may write to
- [ ] Plan writes through the writer the core gives it, never to the file system directly
- [ ] A write outside the listed folders (`..`, absolute path, symlink) fails (covered by `node --test`)
- [ ] Plan's state lives under `.groundwork/plan/`; an existing `.prd-maker/` is moved over and the hook finds it
- [ ] `.groundwork/` is in the repo's `.gitignore`

title: Build reads GitHub issues as tickets
body:
**PRD:** d-local-tickets, n-build-conv, f-build-tickets, f-build-deps

## What to build

Groundwork's own tickets live in GitHub issues, and Build cannot show them today: it reads only local Markdown tickets under `.scratch/`. Build learns to read the project's GitHub issues as tickets: state, milestone, labels, and the "Blocked by" links (GitHub's own dependency links, or a "Blocked by" section in the body). Every existing view (tickets, dependencies, activity, inconsistencies) works with them. Local Markdown tickets keep working.

The restructuring this needs is part of this ticket. Reading tickets (ticket, state, "Blocked by", areas, inconsistencies) is embedded in the Build page today. It moves into a file of its own with one entry point: from a ticket source it returns the ticket model. Local files and GitHub are two sources behind it. The page must still work when opened by double click (`file://`), so this is a plain script, not an ES module, loadable in the browser and under Node.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On the core server Build shows this repo's GitHub issues, with their dependencies and milestones
- [ ] A project with `.scratch/` tickets shows them as before
- [ ] GitHub access goes through the server; no token ends up in the page
- [ ] The ticket reader is a file of its own; the Build page uses it and still works by double click with the folder picker
- [ ] The ticket reader has `node --test` tests through its interface, for both sources (states, the forms of "Blocked by", cross-area references)

title: Records: core record store, with Ideas on it (tracer)
body:
**PRD:** d-rec-store-core, d-record-model, d-rec-common, d-rec-manifest, d-rec-md-source, d-rec-flat, d-rec-layout, d-rec-cache, d-rec-ids-case, d-rec-history-section, d-rec-derived-not-stored, d-rec-sec-writes, d-rec-sec-html, d-rec-idea, d-ideas-new, d-ideas-removed, d-typecheck, d-rec-test-roundtrip, x-rec-per-module, x-rec-json-source

## What to build

The tracer for the record store (C-2, docs/product/records/TECH.md). A shared record store lives in the core: modules declare their record types in a new manifest field `records` (prefix, folder, lifecycle, rules), and the store reads, writes and numbers them. A case record is one Markdown file: front matter plus body, and a `## Történet` (history) list at the end to which the store appends a line (date · who · what) on every lifecycle or link change. The Markdown is the source; the store keeps only a rebuildable JSON cache and index under `.groundwork/` (not in git). Computed data (stage, counts, reverse links) is never written to the files.

Numbers are sequential per prefix and never reused. File names carry a three-digit padded number and a slug (`I-005-….md`), references use the bare id (`I-5`), and the id also stands in the front matter, so renaming a file breaks nothing.

The browser reads records from `/api/records` (list, one record, live updates over the existing events); Claude uses `groundwork record list|show <id>`.

Ideas is the first type on the store: the Ideas module declares type `I` with its folder `docs/product/ideas/` (no longer `ideas/items/`) and the states new · considering · accepted · rejected · snoozed (`until:`) · duplicate (`duplicate: I-n`). The rule that Claude only moves ideas between new and considering is enforced by the store on every write. The board and `groundwork ideas` keep working on top of the store. Accepting an idea is only a state change until C-3: the call to Plan's `/api/plan/todo` goes away (the board's new decision buttons come with C-3).

Type checking starts here: JSDoc types for records and store operations, checked with `tsc --noEmit` at development time (no build step).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A module's `records` declaration is enough for the store to list, read, create and update its records; the store writes only under `docs/product/` and `.groundwork/`
- [ ] Ideas live in `docs/product/ideas/`, and the board, the CLI and the API work as before on top of the store
- [ ] The store refuses a Claude/CLI move outside new ↔ considering (tested)
- [ ] New numbers are never reused, also after a record is deleted (tested)
- [ ] Every lifecycle or link change appends one history line; the history survives a rewrite
- [ ] Deleting `.groundwork/` loses nothing: the index is rebuilt from the Markdown
- [ ] Round trip: read(write(x)) = x and write(read(write(x))) = write(x), byte for byte, for idea records, including generated ones
- [ ] Record Markdown is rendered without raw HTML (tested)
- [ ] `tsc --noEmit` passes on the store; `node --test` passes; no console errors

None - can start immediately

title: Records: Spec documents as canonical Markdown
body:
**PRD:** d-rec-md-source, d-rec-tolerant, d-rec-spec-per-doc, d-rec-parts-file, d-rec-ids-spec, d-rec-history-item, d-superseded, d-rec-skills-read-md, d-spec-structure, d-rec-part, d-rec-doc, d-rec-item, d-plan-dissolves, d-rec-test-roundtrip, d-rec-test-tolerant, x-rec-spec-one

## What to build

The Spec as canonical Markdown, read and written by the record store. Each Spec document is one file: `docs/product/spec/<part>/<KIND>.md`, and the whole system's is `spec/SYSTEM.md`. The parts are listed in `spec/parts.md`, one line per part (name, slug, type, one-sentence description, active / retired).

Inside a document the structure is in readable marks, in one canonical form that the store writes and reads back: sections with `{#t-…}`; item lines carrying the id (`d-…`, `f-…`), status, implementation and origin (`C-7`, later changes, `felváltotta: C-9` when superseded), with note and link below; groups, section prose, the human's own paragraphs and progress. Ids are readable and unique across the whole Spec (`core`, `core/tech`, `d-npm`). An item id stands next to its line, so a `**Spec:**` or `**PRD:**` line can be found with grep. A superseded item stays, marked.

The reader is tolerant: whatever does not fit the canonical form is kept as human text. The next tool write only normalizes the form and never drops content.

Plan's document generator (`documents.mjs`, `doc-strings.mjs`) moves into the store as this writer-reader; documents stay in the document language (hu/en).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `groundwork record show core/tech` (and the API) return a Spec document with its sections and items
- [ ] Round trip byte for byte (read(write(x)) = x, write(read(write(x))) = write(x)) for every Spec document kind, including randomly generated documents
- [ ] A collection of real, hand- or agent-broken files (deleted mark, rewritten item line, free paragraph, git conflict markers, implementation updated by an agent): no content is lost, and every non-canonical line is reported
- [ ] Item ids are unique across the Spec; a superseded item is kept with its marker
- [ ] `node --test` and `tsc --noEmit` pass
